name: Tapentadol
subclass: Opioid agonist with norepinephrine reuptake inhibition
description: Tapentadol (Nucynta) facts: uses, dosing basics, risks, serotonin warnings, interactions, overdose, withdrawal, and legal access in the US.
quick: Tapentadol (Nucynta) is a prescription opioid that also blocks norepinephrine reuptake. It is used for acute pain and, in extended-release form, for chronic pain and diabetic nerve pain. It is a Schedule II controlled substance.
facts: Acute pain (IR); chronic pain and diabetic peripheral neuropathy pain (ER)

profile.medical: Acute and chronic pain; diabetic nerve pain

blocks.p: Immediate-release tapentadol is approved for acute pain severe enough to require an opioid. Extended-release tapentadol is approved for severe chronic pain needing daily treatment and for nerve pain from diabetic peripheral neuropathy.[[1]]
Because it is broken down mainly by glucuronidation rather than CYP enzymes, tapentadol has fewer drug-enzyme interactions than oxycodone or tramadol.

sections.q: What are the risks and side effects of tapentadol?

boxed.title: FDA boxed warnings
items: Tapentadol exposes users to risks of addiction, misuse, and abuse, which can lead to overdose and death.
Life-threatening slowed breathing can occur, especially when starting treatment or after a dose increase.
Accidental ingestion, especially by children, can cause a fatal overdose.
Use with benzodiazepines or other central nervous system depressants, including alcohol, can cause profound sedation, slowed breathing, coma, and death.
Prolonged use during pregnancy can cause neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome, which may be life-threatening if not recognized and treated.

blocks.p: **Common side effects** include nausea, dizziness, vomiting, drowsiness, constipation, and headache. Constipation is often milder than with other opioids.[[1]]
**Serious risks** include slowed breathing, seizures, and serotonin syndrome with serotonergic drugs.[[1]]

sections.q: What does tapentadol overdose look like?

blocks.p: Tapentadol overdose causes pinpoint pupils, extreme drowsiness, slow or stopped breathing, and limpness. Seizures can occur.[[1]][[2]]

emergency.title: If someone may have overdosed
items: Call 911 if the person is unresponsive, cannot be woken, has blue or gray lips, or is breathing slowly or not at all.
Give naloxone (Narcan or a generic nasal spray, sold without a prescription) into one nostril. If there is no response after 2 to 3 minutes, give another dose.
If you are trained, give rescue breaths. Otherwise place the person on their side so they do not choke.
Stay with them. Naloxone can wear off before tapentadol does, so the overdose can return even after the person wakes up.
Most states have Good Samaritan laws that protect people who call 911 for an overdose from some drug charges.

sections.q: What is tapentadol withdrawal like, and how long does it last?

blocks.p: People who take tapentadol regularly for more than a few weeks become physically dependent, even when they take it exactly as prescribed. Dependence is not the same as addiction, but it means stopping suddenly causes withdrawal.[[1]]

timeline.title: Early symptoms
timeline.text: Anxiety, restlessness, yawning, sweating, runny nose, watery eyes, and muscle aches.

timeline.title: Peak withdrawal
timeline.text: Diarrhea, stomach cramps, nausea and vomiting, goosebumps, dilated pupils, fast heartbeat, and strong cravings. Rarely dangerous in healthy adults, but dehydration can be serious.

timeline.title: Lingering symptoms
timeline.text: Poor sleep, low mood, low energy, and cravings can continue for weeks. Tolerance falls quickly, which raises the risk of overdose if use restarts.

blocks.warn: After a break, the body loses tolerance within days. Returning to a previous dose of tapentadol can cause a fatal overdose.

blocks.p: The FDA warns against stopping opioids abruptly in people who are physically dependent. A prescriber can taper the dose gradually, often by 10% or less per month for long-term users, and medicines such as clonidine or lofexidine can ease symptoms. For opioid use disorder, buprenorphine and methadone cut the risk of death roughly in half.[[3]]

sections.q: How do you get tapentadol legally in the US?

blocks.p: In the United States, tapentadol is a Schedule II controlled substance. The only legal way to get it is with a prescription from a clinician registered with the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), filled by a licensed pharmacy. Depending on state law, that can be a physician, nurse practitioner, or physician assistant.[[4]]

ul: **Refills:** Schedule II prescriptions cannot be refilled. A prescriber can write several prescriptions at once, with dates when each may be filled, for up to a 90-day supply in total.[[5]]

**Telehealth:** federal flexibilities let DEA-registered clinicians prescribe Schedule II to V medicines after a telemedicine visit, without a prior in-person exam, through December 31, 2026. A permanent DEA rule was under final review in late 2026. State rules can be stricter.[[6]]
**Monitoring:** prescribers and pharmacists in most states check a prescription drug monitoring program, a database of controlled-substance prescriptions, before prescribing or dispensing.

**Pharmacies:** a legitimate pharmacy always requires a valid prescription, has a licensed pharmacist available, and is licensed in the state it ships to. The FDA's BeSafeRx tool and the NABP's safe pharmacy list help confirm a pharmacy is real.[[7]][[8]]
**Cost:** tapentadol is brand-only in the US and costly; many insurers require prior authorization.

blocks.p: **Traveling:** keep the medicine in its original pharmacy container and carry a copy of the prescription. Check the rules of the destination country before travel, because many countries restrict controlled medicines or require a permit.

Yes, but only with a valid prescription and only from a pharmacy licensed in your state. Many licensed pharmacies, including mail-order pharmacies run by insurers, fill tapentadol prescriptions online and ship them. Buying tapentadol from a website that does not require a prescription is illegal, and the product is often fake.[[7]][[9]]

The prescription goes to a pharmacy
Prescriptions for controlled medicines are usually sent electronically, straight from the prescriber to the pharmacy you choose.
The pharmacy checks and fills it
A pharmacist verifies the prescription and your identity, then dispenses the medicine in person or by mail.

blocks.p: **Signs that an online seller is illegal:**

ul: It sells tapentadol with no prescription, or after only a short online questionnaire.
It takes orders through social media, messaging apps, or email.
It asks for payment in cryptocurrency, gift cards, or money transfers.
It has no US street address, no state pharmacy license, and no pharmacist to speak to.
Its prices are far below those of ordinary pharmacies, or it ships from another country.

blocks.p: The FDA's BeSafeRx tool links to each state's license lookup, and the National Association of Boards of Pharmacy lists verified online pharmacies.[[7]][[8]]

faq: Yes. Tapentadol is a stronger opioid and is Schedule II, while tramadol is Schedule IV.
Studies show somewhat less constipation than equally effective doses of oxycodone, but it can still occur.
Is there a generic for Nucynta?
As of 2026, tapentadol is sold in the US mainly as the brand Nucynta.
How long does tapentadol stay in your system?
Its half-life is about 4 hours, and most is cleared within a day.
